LESSON: READING 6.2.1 READING FLUENCY: POETRY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.2: Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we read poems fluently?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read poems with correct pace and intonation for self - expression
2. answer oral questions from a poem for comprehension
3. recite poems based on the theme for enjoyment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 6.2.1 READING FLUENCY: POETRY
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 6.2.1 READING FLUENCY: POETRY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read poems with correct pace and intonation for self - expression

What this means
In this part you learn to read poems with correct pace and intonation for self - expression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read poems with correct pace and intonation for self - expression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read poems with correct pace and intonation for self - expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Answer oral questions from a poem for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to answer oral questions from a poem for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: answer oral questions from a poem for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can answer oral questions from a poem for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Recite poems based on the theme for enjoyment

What this means
In this part you learn to recite poems based on the theme for enjoyment. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recite poems based on the theme for enjoyment.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recite poems based on the theme for enjoyment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read poems with correct pace and intonation for self - expression)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry to a partner. (skill: answer oral questions from a poem for comprehension)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: recite poems based on the theme for enjoyment)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read poems with correct pace and intonation for self - expression.
3. Practise this skill: answer oral questions from a poem for comprehension.
4. Practise this skill: recite poems based on the theme for enjoyment.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we read poems fluently?
2. Why are poems important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: Poetry means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read poems with correct pace and intonation for self - expression.
5. Be able to: answer oral questions from a poem for comprehension.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
